title: Microgravity combustion evidence for spacecraft and habitat atmospheres
purpose_example: Make informed decisions about fire safety in a lunar habitat, with respect to flames in microgravity
subject: combustion tests
byline: Synthesised from NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) experiment tables
disclaimer: Prometeo compares conditions; it does not predict whether a material ignites or a flame spreads. Data: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (psi.nasa.gov), CC0. Not an official NASA product.
footer: Prometeo · NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Flame in Freefall

presets.label: Lunar base
presets.blurb: Oxygen-enriched, reduced-pressure cabin atmosphere (30 % O₂ at 10.2 psi), chosen to shorten pre-breathe before surface excursions.
presets.source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge statement (30 % O₂, 10.2 psi); material is an example value

presets.label: Space station
presets.blurb: Earth-like cabin atmosphere (21 % O₂ at 14.7 psi) in microgravity.
presets.source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge statement (14.7 psi); material is an example value

presets.label: Spacesuit
presets.blurb: Pure oxygen at very low pressure (100 % O₂ at 4.3 psi).
presets.source: NASA Space Apps 2026, Flame in Freefall challenge statement (100 % O₂, 4.3 psi); material is an example value

known_gaps.note: No record in this corpus was taken at partial gravity: every flight investigation ran in microgravity.

outcome_columns_note: Outcome columns are kept verbatim; their formats differ between investigations.
